rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the ever-living witness whose knowledge misses nothing and whose permission governs all things; His universal mercy reaches creation and His special mercy favors His devoted servants.
rows.anchor: لا يعزب شيء عن علمه ، ولا يكون شيء إلا بإذنه ، الرحمن الرحيم الذي عمت رحمته الموجودات

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل محمد المشدالي المغربي
rows.claim: Al-Mashdali's method for Qur'anic coherence is to identify a surah's purpose, its prerequisites and their distance from the goal, then answer expectations raised as the discourse unfolds.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا الإمام المحقق أبو الفضل محمد بن العلامة القدوة أبي عبد الله محمد ابن العلامة القدوة أبي القاسم محمد المشدالي المغربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A surah's name summarizes its purpose, as a title signals the details within; Adam demonstrated this naming principle when he named things before the angels.
rows.anchor: أن اسم كل سورة مترجم عن مقصودها هلأن أسم كل شيء تظهر المناسبة بينه وبين مسماه عنوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha's many titles converge on مراقبة: it is the Mother of the Book, foundation, oft-repeated, treasure, healing, sufficing, complete, protecting, incantation, praise, thanks, supplication and prayer.
rows.anchor: فمدار هذه الأسماء كما ترى على أمر خفي كاف لكل مراد وهو المراقبة التي سأقول إنها مقصودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha is a treasure, cure, sufficiency, fulfillment, protection and incantation; it gathers praise, gratitude and supplication, with prayer as their greatest assembly.
rows.anchor: فكل شيء لا يفتتح بها لا اعتداد به ، وهي كنز لكل شيء شافية لكل داء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha's purpose is to establish God's exclusive right to all praise and perfection, sovereignty over both worlds, worship and aid, and to ask for the path of the successful rather than the doomed; its center is مراقبة.
rows.anchor: الغرض الذي سبقت له الفاتحة وه إثبات استحقاق الله تعالى لجميع المحامد وصفا الكمال ، واختصاصه بملك الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets, scriptures and laws ultimately gather people to truth so they may know their sovereign and what pleases Him; knowledge and practice together serve the Qur'an's purpose.
rows.anchor: لأن المقصود منت إرسال الرسل وإنزال الكتب نصب الشرائع ، والمقصود من نصب الشرائع جمع الخلق على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's name should accompany every movement and stillness because it leads to مراقبة, fear and recognition that affairs begin and end with Him, so the Fatiha opens with the basmala.
rows.anchor: وكان اتزام اسمه تعالى في كل حركة وسكون قائدا إلى مراقبته وداعيا إلى مخافته واعتقاد أن مصادر الأمور ومواردها منه وإليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior refuge seeks to clear the reciter's inner life and focus scattered concerns; the basmala's opening and closing letters symbolize return in worldly governance, death in the intermediate realm and resurrection.
rows.anchor: جعلت البسملة كلها للمعاد لأبتدائها بحرف شفوي ، وختام أول كلماتها ومآخرها بآخر إشارة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali glosses the basmala: باء manifests causal wisdom; ism reveals what is hidden to hearts through hearing; Allah names the one hearts seek beyond reason; Rahman is universally merciful and Rahim grants mercy approved by divinity.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في تفسيره في غريب ألفاظ البسملة : الباء معناها أظهره الله سبحانه من حكمة التسبيب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the basmala shows that all things proceed through God's name alone, folding apparent causes back to Him; it should therefore begin people's words and deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال في غريب معناها : لما أظهر الله سبحانه حكمة التسبيب وأرى الخلق استفادة بعض الأشياء من أشياء أخر متقدمة عليها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The basmala relates to the Fatiha as the Fatiha relates to the Qur'an: each is a compact synthesis of what the larger whole details.
rows.anchor: وأشد منه أنه لما كانت نسبة البسملة من الفاتحة نسبة الفاتحة من القرآن صدرت بها الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is a proper name encompassing all beautiful names; Rahman precedes Rahim because it is exclusive and more emphatic, following the order of existence, general mercy, then worship-specific mercy.
rows.anchor: ولما كان اسم الجلالة علما وكان جامعا لجميع معاني الأسماء الحسنى أولية الرحمن من حيث أنه كالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mercy names affirm that God deserves these attributes intrinsically, fit His lordship and sovereignty, and show mercy prevailing over wrath; universal mercy also excludes every defect.
rows.anchor: وكررهما بعهد تنبيها عل وجوب ذلك للربوبية والملك وللدلالة على أن الرحمة غلبت الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala has nineteen written and eighteen spoken letters, alluding to the nineteen guardians of Hell and to mercy drawn by the five prayers and witr.
rows.anchor: وكونها تسعة عشر حرفا خطية وثمانية عشر لفظية إشارة إلى أنها دوافع النقمة من النار التي أصحابها تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the basmala is a kind of praise, it naturally leads to comprehensive al-hamd: begin affairs by praising God as the one deserving every praise, with hope and awe guiding the way.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت البسملة نوعا من الحمد ناسب كل المناسبة تعقيبها باسم الحمد ةالكلي الجامع لجميع أفراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hamd lillah establishes that God deserves praise for His essence and perfection; Rabb al-alamin adds His lordship, sovereignty and beneficence, while the worlds point to creation's beginning and the inference to resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما أثبت بقوله : { الحمد لله } أنه المستحق لجميع المحامد لا لشىء غير ذاته الحائز لجميع الكمالات أشار إلى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines al-hamd as complete praise covering all actions and attributes, all from God and free of blame; its definite form signals praise reaching its full extent.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : و { الحمد } المدح الكامل الذي يحيط بجميع الأفعال والأوصاف , على أن جميعها إنما هو من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lordship does not yield wellbeing without mercy, so Rahman and Rahim follow al-hamd and encourage people to persist in praising God.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت مرتبة الربوبية لا تستجمع الصلاح إل بالرحمة اتبع ذلك بصفتي { الرحمن الرحيم } ترغبيا

rows.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali's principle that the Qur'an contains no repetition prompts a further explanation for repeating Rahman and Rahim.
rows.anchor: عن الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي رحمه الله تعالى أنه لا مكرر في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A merciful Lord might lack sovereign power, so the Fatiha adds Master of the Day of Judgment, whose majestic force inspires fear.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الرب المنعوت بالرمحة قد لايكون مالكاوكانت الربوبية لاتتم إلا بالملك المفيد للعزة المقرون بابلهيبة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines a day as the span in which an outward affair is completed; Judgment Day outwardly runs from resurrection to eternity, while inwardly it begins when sin's effects and recompense meet.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ولايوم مقدار ما يتم فيه أمر ظاهر , ثم قال : و { يوم الدين } في الظاهر هو يوم الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recompense does not truly wait until the afterlife: sin leaves a dark mark in the heart, and worldly calamities are God's recompense even when people blame custom or other people.
rows.anchor: ولذلك يؤثر عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إن العبد إذا أذنب نكت في قلبه نكتة سوداء )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says fever comes from Hell's pus and severe heat and cold are from it, presenting earthly illness as recompense.
rows.anchor: كما وردعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الحمى من قيح جهنم , وإن شدة الحر والقر من نفسها )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls illness God's scourge on earth, by which He disciplines His servants; grief, worry, anxiety and greed also punish the soul.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( المرض سوط الله في الأرض يؤدب به عبادة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all worldly and otherworldly recompense returns to God, He is sovereign and owner of the Day of Judgment and its full course.
rows.anchor: وهو تعالى بمقتضى ذلك كله ملك يوم الدين ومالكه يوم الدين ومالكه مطلقافي الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases about recompense according to people's descriptions and deeds complete the account of God's supreme glory, echoed by the sacred report My servant glorified Me.
rows.anchor: وبه تم انتهاء الشرف العلي وهو المجد الذي عبر عنه قوله تعالى : ( مجدني عبدي ) انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings, Malik and Maalik, are transmitted and convey the same sovereignty: ownership of the Day entails exclusive control over everything in it.
rows.anchor: ولنا لم يكن فرق هما في الدلالة على الملك بين قراءة ( ملك ) وقراءة ( مالك ) جاءت الرواية بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding ownership to the Day gives the full meaning of kingship, unlike adding it to people; hence there is no variant reading in King of people.
rows.anchor: ولما لم تفد إضافة إلى الناس هذا المعنى لم يكن خلاف في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's worthiness and prompting hope and fear, the recitation turns from third person to direct address and puts the means before the request.
rows.anchor: فلما استجمع الأمر استحقاقا وتحبيبا وترغيبا وترهيبا كان من شأن كل ذي لب الإقبال إليه وقصر الهمم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyyaka addresses the possessor of these attributes, and worship means reaching the utmost abasement; repeating the pronoun intensifies the request for aid.
rows.anchor: أي يا من هذه الصفات صفاته { نعبد } كما قال الحالي : تبلغ الغاية في أنحاء التذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is possible only through God's aid, and guidance lies in His hand; the sequence moves from essence to acts to attributes and back to essence, teaching dependence after recognizing God's right.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن عبادته لا تتهيأ إلا بمعونته وإلى أن ملاك الهداية بيده

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet seeking refuge in God's pardon from punishment, pleasure from anger, and God from God, then admitting he cannot enumerate His praise.
rows.anchor: والنسائى وهذا لفظة في التعود عن عائشة رضى الله عنها : ( أعوذ بعوفك من عقوبتك , وبرضاك من سخطك

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says all Qur'an is God's speech, but some verses voice what creatures at different levels ought to say yet cannot express; God teaches them words that fulfill their duty.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أى هذه وما بهدها مما جاء كلام الله فيه جارياعلى لسان خلقه فإن القرآن كله كلام الله

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali explains the sound report that God divided prayer between Himself and His servant: the first three verses are God's praise, which He accepts from the reciting servant as praise and glorification.
rows.anchor: وتلك هي صلاتهم المقسمة التى عبر عنها فيما صح عنه علية الصلاة والسلام من قوله تعالى : ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the paired verse belongs between God and servant: worship is the servant's commitment, aid is God's gift, and aid precedes and enables worship.
rows.anchor: فكان ظاهرهاغ التزام عهد العبادة وهو ما يرجع إلى العبد وعمادها طلب المعونة من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Whoever asks God for aid with a genuine task receives help proportionate to it; failure comes from neglecting God's due, misunderstanding the verse or forgetting its favor, and the plural nun signals congregational prayer.
rows.anchor: فمن كانت عليه مؤنة شىء فاستعان الله فيهالا على مقتضى هذه الآية جاءته المعونة على قدر مؤنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches confession of inability, need and reliance on God's power; that dependence leads directly to asking for guidance along the necessary path.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية ندب إلى اعتقاد العجز واستشعار الافتقار والاعتصام بحوله وقوته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines the condemned as those who intentionally oppose guidance and thereby incur divine wrath, or those who turn toward guidance then stray without intending to.
rows.anchor: وأما من هدى وجهة ما فضل عن مرجععها فهو ضلال مذموم لأنه ضالال بعد هدى وهو يكون عن اعوجاج في الجبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested path is that of God's messengers; because blessing reaches every creature, the request seeks the mercy-specific path of those honored by God, not merely existence.
rows.anchor: فأشار إلى أن الاعتصام به في اتباع رسله , ولما كان سبحانه عام النعمة لكل موجود عدواكان أو وليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the object of bestowed favor broadens the wording; the negation excludes the angry and astray as separate failures, one in action and the other in knowledge.
rows.anchor: وان حذف المنعم به لإرادة التعميم من باب تقليل اللفظ لتكثير المعنى فكان من المعلوم أن محط السؤال بعض أهل دمشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the angry as a group that rejects action obstinately and the astray as a group deprived of felicity through failure in knowledge, warning against both.
rows.anchor: فعرف أنهم قسمان : قسم أريد للشقاوة فعاند في إخلاله بالعمل فاستوجب الغضب , وقسم لم يرد للسعادة فضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using غير rather than an exception marks exclusion from the outset, making clear that the requested universal blessing means the special honor granted to the faithful, not the general gift of existence.
rows.anchor: فعرف أن المسؤول إنما هو طريق أهل النعمة بصفة الرحيمية تشوقت النفوس إلى معرفتهم فميزهم ببيان أضدادهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the condemned intentionally show defiance, while the astray turn toward guidance and deviate without intending it; Amin expresses a decisive plea for a response.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : { المغضوب عليهم } الذين ظهر منهم المراغمة وتعمد الخالفة فيوجب ذلك الغضب من الأعلى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Amin means the petitioner trusts God not to reject the plea, since nothing can overcome or restrain Him; the word asks Him to respond.
rows.anchor: آمين كلمة عزم من الأمن , مدلولها أن المدعو مأمون منه أن يرد من دعاه لأنه لايعجز شىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's arrangement is miraculous, so the Fatiha must retain its required order in prayer; rearrangement or insertion of foreign material invalidates it. Al-Isfahani locates its clearest inimitability in order.
rows.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين الإعجاز يتعلق بالنظم والترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual seeker passes through awe of God's attributes, recognizes many perilous paths and the lack of guidance or safety apart from God, then asks for the straight path, its blessed companions and protection from both condemned groups.
rows.anchor: فلما أشرف وستنار وعرف مواقع الأسرار بالأقدار كأنه قيل له : ماذا تطلب وفي أي مذهب تذهب ؟

rows.speaker: مسعود التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftazani maps the Fatiha's blessings to two creations and two preservations: creation in Rabb al-alamin, preservation in mercy, second creation in judgment, and afterlife preservation in worship onward.
rows.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فغنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء ثانيافي دار الفناء والبقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root and forms of al-hamd suggest reaching an end, extension, encompassing and circularity; these imply lowering the head and can lead to contentment and gratitude.
rows.anchor: وهذا يرجع إلى أصل مدلول الحمد فإن مادته بكل ترتيب تدور على بلغوغ الغاية ويلزم منه الاتساع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the seven repeated verses are the Qur'an's gathered essence and its contents will be disclosed at creation's completion; earlier scriptures progress from changeable scrolls and lasting books to the Qur'an, which completes religion.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب القفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في أخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali contrasts the Qur'an's detailed, dispersed sequence with the Fatiha's seven complete universals, and makes the Fatiha a mirror of the servant's move from misguidance to guidance.
rows.anchor: ووجه فوت أم القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع , فيه نجوم مبثوثة غير منتظمة , وحداة إثر واحدة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says he was sent to complete noble character; the author links this completion with the Fatiha's comprehensive opening and the Qur'an's culmination.
rows.anchor: بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق . أن إلى ربك المنتهى .

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's majesty through rulings spanning immediate and deferred realities, witnessed experience, and reports of the past and patterns that recur in time.
rows.anchor: ومن مجيده وهو ما حربت أحكامه من بين عاجل ما شهد وآجل ما علم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual descent that moves understanding between states and rulings from descent from high to low, which may occur with or without intermediaries.
rows.anchor: وما كان منه بتدريج وتقريب للأفهام ففاءت من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage names al-Baqara 2:281 as the last revealed verse and says its recitation position between the debt verse and the verse before it shows revelation and recitation order can differ.
rows.anchor: وجعلوها بين آية الدين والآية قبلها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an's sevenfold gathering in Muhammad's heart relates to the Mother of Qur'an's universals as the Qur'an's gathering in his heart relates to the Mother.
rows.anchor: وأما الجمع ففي قلبه نسبة جوامعه السبع في أم القرآن إلى القرآن بمنزلة نسبة جمعه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an reached the Prophet on his tongue over the span of the prophetic mission, after its descent to the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: وعلى لسانه في أمد أيام النبوة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that Muhammad's character was the Qur'an, making his conduct the visible form of its inner reality.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother: its first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, while its last three cover the creature's way to God, mercy or failure.
rows.anchor: فالآيات الثلاث الول قال شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Recitation order can differ from revelation chronology; the verse allowing the Prophet to marry certain women was placed before a later restriction.
rows.anchor: فقد يتطابق قرآن الأمر وتطور الخلق وقد لا يتابق والله يتولى إقامتها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the authentic report in Muslim and the four Sunan, God says the Fatiha is divided between Himself and His servant: He answers praise, glorification and worship, and grants the servant's final requests.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال : سمعت زسول الله صلى اله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara aims to prove the Book is guidance to follow; belief in the unseen, especially resurrection and the afterlife, is its greatest guidance and organizing theme.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إقامة الدليل على أن الكتاب هدى ليتبع يفي كل ما قال ، وأعظم ما يهدي إليه الإيمالن بالغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cow story makes the surah's title apt because resurrection occurs through an apparently slight human cause; it is a clearer sign of divine power than Abraham's story or earlier Israelite resurrections.
rows.anchor: فلذلك سميت بها السورة وكانت بذلك أحق من قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنها في نوع البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following comparison of hearts and stones shows the guided and astray: hearts become hard and wretched, while stones display fear and yield benefit that reaches God's servants.
rows.anchor: ولا سيما وقد اتبعت بوصف القلوب والحجارة بما عم اللمهتدين بالكتاب والضالين فوصفها بالقسوة الموجبة للشقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book functions like a caliph from the resolute messengers, guiding every matter to the right exit: rejecting it fails, hesitation nearly perishes, and accepting it brings piety and excellence.
rows.anchor: وفيها إشارة إلى أن هذا الكتاب فينا كما لو كان فينا خليفة من أولي العزم من الرسل يرشدنا في كل أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara is also called the Radiant and the Hump: it illuminates guidance and sufficiency, brightens believers' faces at judgment, and exalts belief in the afterlife above every other good after monotheism.
rows.anchor: وسميت الزهراء لإنارتها طريق الهداية والكفاية في الدنيا والآخرة ، ولأيجابها إسفار الوجوه يفي يوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali transmits a report attributed to the Prophet from Ibn Masud: earlier books came through one gate and letter, whereas the Qur'an came through seven gates and seven letters encompassing commands, prohibitions, rulings, ambiguities and parables.
rows.anchor: قال العلامة أبو الحسن الحرالي في كتاب العروة لمفتاح الباب المقفل في معنى ما رواه عن ابن وهب من حديث ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says the seven-letter report is unestablished: Abu Salama did not meet Ibn Masud, his son Salama is not authoritative, and its chain is agreed to be weak; Ahmad ibn Abi Imran also rejected it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر : هذا الحديث عند أهل الحديث لم يثبت ، وأبو سلمة لم يلق ابن مسعود ، وابنه سلمة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits an alternative mursal route through al-Layth, Uqayl, Ibn Shihab, Umm Salama and Abu Salama; he calls the mursal report good because Abu Salama did not meet Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: قال أبو شامة : وهكذا رواه البيهقي في كتاب المدخل وقال : هذا مرسل جيد ، أبو سلمة لم يدرك ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama says that if sound, seven letters means seven forms or categories of Qur'anic content, not the dialects in which recitation was permitted.
rows.anchor: قال أبو شامة : وهكذا رواه البيهقي في كتاب المدخل وقال : هذا مرسل جيد

rows.speaker: ابن الجزري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazari cites the Prophet's report to Ibn Masud from al-Tabarani: the Qur'an's seven categories include lawful, forbidden, clear, ambiguous, parables, commands and warnings, each with its proper response.
rows.anchor: محمد ابن الجزري الدمشقي الشافعي في أوائل كتابه ' النشر في القراءات العشر ' إلى الطبراني

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi also reports from Abu Huraira a version that describes five Qur'anic forms: lawful, forbidden, clear, ambiguous and parables.
rows.anchor: ورواه البيهقي في فضل القرآن من الشعب عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه بلفظ

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali reads the seven letters as a completion of creation and religious, worldly and afterlife well-being: Muhammad is the comprehensive final prophet and his book seals the scriptures; he cites the report I was sent to complete noble character.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : زفي حديث آخر من طريق ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : إن الكتب كانت تنزل من باب واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted supplication asks God to set right religion as the safeguard of one's affairs, worldly livelihood and the afterlife to which one returns.
rows.anchor: اللهم أصلح لي ديني الذي هو عصمة أمري

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali divides the three domains of well-being into action and restraint, yielding six letters; God then grants Muhammad a seventh, inclusive letter, so the Qur'an descends in seven letters.
rows.anchor: فلما استوفى الستة وهبه ربه حرفا جامعا سابعا فردا لا زوج له ن فتم إنزاله على سبعة أحرف .

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The worldly pair is halal and haram: lawful things cultivate body and soul, forbidden things must be purified away; the pair originates in the Torah and is completed in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فأدنى تلك الحروف هو حرف إصلاح الدنيا ، فلها حرفان ، أحدهما : حرف الحرام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The afterlife pair is warning and command; avoiding prohibitions purifies and obeying commands advances the next life, even when it sacrifices temporary worldly benefits for enduring whole good.
rows.anchor: ثم يلي هذين حرفا صلاح المعاد : أحدهما حرف الزجر والنهي التي لا تصلح الآخرة إلا بالتطهير منه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The religious pair is clear guidance about heart, character and bodily duties, and ambiguous matters beyond limited reason that require declaring God incomparable; five letters are for practice and the sixth for restraint.
rows.anchor: ثم يلي هذين حرفا صلاح الدين : أحدهما حرف المحكم الذي بان للعبد فيه خطاب ربه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The six letters are shared with prior scriptures but perfected in the Qur'an; its unique seventh is the inclusive letter of praise, gifted directly to Muhammad and embodied in his heart, recitation and character.
rows.anchor: فهذه الحروف الستة يشترك فيها القرآن مع سائر الكتب ويزيد عليها تمامها وبركة جمعها ، ويختص القرآن بالحرف السابع الجامع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Because praise is the seventh inclusive letter, the Fatiha begins with it and gathers the seven universals diffused through the Qur'an, as the Qur'an gathers earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: ولما كان حرف الحمد هو سابعها الجامع افتتح الله به سبحانه وتعالى الفاتحة أم القرآن وأم الكتاب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The first verse contains praise's seventh letter; the second contains the lawful and forbidden letters that Rahmaniyyah establishes for worldly life, allowing enjoyment and removing either prohibition's burden or sin.
rows.anchor: فالآية الأولى تشتمل على حرف الحمد السابع ، والثانية تشتمل على حرفي الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Alternatively, and the author says this is likelier, Rahmaniyyah universally grants blessings and removes harms whether for felicity or misery, while Rahimiyyah specifically gives the blessings and protection that lead to felicity.
rows.anchor: وأما الرحيمية فطهرتهم من مضار أبدانهم ورجاسة نفوسهم ومجهلة قلوبهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The third verse contains the sovereign's command, represented by the letters of command and prohibition that appear in religion.
rows.anchor: والآية الثالثة تشتمل على أمر المللك القيم على حرفي الأمر والنهي اللذين ييبدو أمرهما في الدين

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The fourth verse contains the clear letter in worship and the ambiguous letter in seeking help; because it is intimate direct address, its request is not repeated.
rows.anchor: والرابعة تشتمل على حرفي المحكم في قوله ^ ( إياك نعبد ) ^ [ الفاتحة : 5 ]

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The fifth verse's request returns to praise, the sixth to the grace of lawful and forbidden provisions, and the seventh to the sovereign's command; together these complete all seven letters.
rows.anchor: وعادتت مسألة الآيةى الخاتمسة على حرف الحمد ومسألة الآية السادسة على آية النعمة من حرفي الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Qur'an begins with the sixth, ambiguous letter so confessing ignorance and believing without grasping it invites divine gift; this trains compliance with the rest without claiming mastery.
rows.anchor: ولما ابتئت الفاتحة أم القرآن بالسابع الجامع الموهوب ابتدئ القرآن بالحرف السادس المعجوز عنه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: After the ambiguous opening, the Qur'an presents the clear letter in the traits of believers; observance from faith is clear guidance, while external compliance without faith remains mere command.
rows.anchor: ثم ولى السادس المفتتح به القرآن الخامس المحكم كم وجه في قوله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Qur'an's recited order differs from revelation order: the first revelation to the Prophet was the clear command to read, while the first public warning was the command to rise and warn of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وأما تنزيله يفي ترتيب البيان فإن أ , ل ما نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو حرف المحكم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The warning came first for the community because afterlife reform is most important and also sets worldly affairs right; the Prophet rendered warning and prohibition with one sense, though the first addresses instinct and the second understanding.
rows.anchor: فابتدأ سبحانه وتعالى ترتيل الأمة بإصلاح المعاد الأهم لأن عليه يصلح أمر الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr argues that the disconnected letters challenge opponents to use the remaining half of the alphabet to produce a rival discourse; al-Zarkashi transmits the claim.
rows.anchor: نقل ذلك الزركشي في البرهان عن القاضي أبي بكر قال : وقد علم ذلك بعض أرباب الحقائق

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr says every book has an essence and the Qur'an's essence lies in the opening letters of its surahs; Ali likewise calls the alphabetic openings the Qur'an's selected core.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه : في كل كتا بسر وسر الله في القرآن أوائل السور

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim reads Alif-Lam-Mim as the three articulation zones in order, symbolizing creation, worldly life and its laws, and resurrection; the Qur'an gathers what all humanity needs.
rows.anchor: وأبدى الإمام شمس الدين ابن فقيم الجوزيه الدمشقي الحنبلي يفي كتاب به كالتذكرة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali gives metaphysical senses to Alif, Lam and Mim: encompassing authority, the link between hidden and manifest, and the perfected manifestation, with examples including Adam, angels and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي في تفسيره : ' الف ' اسم للقائم الأعلى المحيط ثم لكل مستخلف في القيام كآدم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says these signs are names when pronounced as alif, lam and mim; they are called letters only as word-parts without separate meaning, following al-Khalil's account of their names.
rows.anchor: فينبغي أن يقال فيها أسماء وإن كانمت غير معلومة الدلالة كحروف ألف باء تاء فإنها كلها أسماء على ما فهمه الخليل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the alphabetic openings are the roots of God's first speech, translated into Arabic words and composed as the clear Qur'an; in heavenly scripture they signify the whole before its detailed unfolding.
rows.anchor: وأما حقيقتها فهي جوامع أصلها في ذمر أول من كلام الله تعالى فنزلت إلى الكلم العربية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Their comprehensive signs span existence from its hidden center to visible and audible revelation, and they did not appear in earlier books because creation was then incomplete; the final, complete Book fulfills their promised appearance.
rows.anchor: ولأجل ما اقتضته من الجمع لم تنزل يفي كتاب متقدم لأن كتا بكل وقت مطابق بحال الكون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara answers the Fatiha's plea for guidance by directing worshippers to the Book, describing the guided and denied groups as patterns to follow or avoid; its pious are the straight path and its others the path of ruin.
rows.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو أنه لما أخبلا سبحانه وتعالى أن عباده المخلصين سألوا في الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the surah's purpose is solely to describe the Book; it establishes the truth of its meaning, exposes disbelief and hypocrisy to show that inward faith matters, then proves its inimitable form and authority for teaching law.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت قلت : مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك فتوابع ولوازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the servants' schemes, the surah commands the Prophet to declare God free of their foul claims; the account of creation and guidance then displays divine power and wisdom and exposes their error.
rows.anchor: وكان وقوع ذلك من العبيد المحاط بأعمالهم ودقائق أنفاسهم وأحوالهم من أقبح مرتكب وأبعده عن المعرفة بشيء من عظيم أمر الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates and proportionately forms; He assigns each thing its kinds, individuals, measures, qualities, actions and lifespans, fitting striking to the hand, walking to the leg, hearing to the ear and sight to the eye.
rows.anchor: أي أوقع تقديره في أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأشخاصها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها , وغير ذلك من أحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance follows His apportionment by fitting substances, forms and properties to natural or chosen purposes, creating inclinations and inspirations and setting signs to repel harm and bring benefit; even newborns seek milk instinctively.
rows.anchor: فهدى } أي أوقع بسبب تقديره وعقبه الهداية لذلك الذي وقع التقدير من أجله من الشكل والجواهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation requires proportion to achieve balance, and apportionment requires guidance to achieve completeness.
rows.anchor: فالخالق لا بد له من التسوية ليحصل الاعتدال , والتقدير لا بد له من الهداية ليحصل الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With signs within the self already given, vegetation supplies the strongest horizon sign of resurrection: God brings out grazing plants through rain clouds, first and again.
rows.anchor: وكان النبات من آياتها أدل المخلوقات على البعث قال : { والذي أخرج }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of the dead is no harder for God than gathering and restoring plants after they break down into soil, so pasture demonstrates His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: لأنه سبحانه وتعالى أقدر على جمع الأموات من الأرض بنفسه بعد أن تفتتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pasture's drying and darkening after greenness displays God's complete power and choice through the alternation of opposites in the same substance; غثاء is its scattered, dried debris and أحوى its darkening color.
rows.anchor: ولما كان إيباسه وتسويده بعد اخضراره ونموه في غاية الدلالة على تمام القدرة وكمال الاختيار بمعاقبة الأضداد
